explanation: In C++, class templates allow the creation of generic classes that can operate with any data type. Specialization of class templates enables providing specific implementations for particular types, optimizing behavior or providing type-specific information. The std::numeric_limits class template is a standard example, offering compile-time properties and limits for numeric types. It is used to query characteristics such as the minimum, maximum, or whether a type is signed, facilitating portable and type-safe numeric computations.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of the std::numeric_limits class template to query properties of the int type. It shows that numeric_limits<int> is specialized (as indicated by is_specialized being true) and retrieves the minimum and maximum values for int at compile time. This exemplifies how class template specialization provides type-specific information, enabling portable and efficient numeric computations in C++.
